products.name: Recraft
products.note: Vector image generation; brand consistency; commercial design; UK-hosted

reading.body:
Recraft operates a UK-hosted text-to-image platform focused on vector generation and commercial design, competing in the crowded image synthesis market without apparent regulatory filings or patent activity.

The company's positioning emphasizes brand consistency tooling, a practical lever for teams working across multiple designs. Vector generation is a narrower target than photorealism, reducing compute demand per inference while serving a discrete commercial need. Custom style templates from user-supplied images suggest a fine-tuning or adaptation layer, which could lock users into the platform if styles accumulate value over time.

The absence of SEC filings, litigation records, or MCP server registrations tells you nothing about Recraft's funding, business model, or integration depth. UK hosting is noted but whether this reflects data residency preference, regulatory choice, or cost is not specified. The data does not cover compute infrastructure, training cost, or power consumption, so you cannot infer how much computational demand Recraft places on the grid or how it scales with user growth.

profile_text.body:
Recraft is an AI-powered design platform aimed at designers, creatives, sellers, and teams. The company describes itself as a top-ranked text-to-image model and design platform, offering tools for photorealism, vector generation, custom styles, and mockups. Users can generate and edit images, vectors, and mockups using Recraft's own models alongside other frontier models.

The platform's core product, also called Recraft, focuses on brand consistency and commercial design use cases, with vector image generation as a notable capability. The site highlights a custom style feature that allows users to drop in their own images and convert them into reusable, editable styles. The product is noted as UK-hosted.

The site holds a verified profile for Recraft dated September 2026. No litigation, SEC filings, MCP server registrations, or patent records are present in the available data.
